correctness.rationale: For each diagonal SPD metric the symmetric similarity transform is a nonnegative symmetric four-vertex path with squared edges q_i=p_i/p_{i+1}. Strict Perron monotonicity forces extremal endpoint weights. At fixed central ratio s=p_3/p_2, the product q_1q_3 and q_2 are fixed; the exact characteristic polynomial shows the Perron eigenvalue increases with q_1+q_3, so AM-GM uniquely balances the outer edges, with a feasible equality metric for every s. The remaining one-variable Perron eigenvalue has an explicitly differentiated sign controlled by K r^3=2, proving the unique phase-change minimizer. Substitution gives the two formulas for R(K). The logarithmic norm derivative at t=0 makes the weighted semigroup nonexpansion criterion an iff, and monotone inversion gives the three sharp conditioning thresholds. A rational K=16 witness has a congruent symmetric certificate with spectrum 0,-1,-3,-4, replayed by the standalone exact checker.

originality.rationale: Classical positive-systems theory establishes existence of some diagonal Lyapunov function for every Hurwitz Metzler matrix; this is not claimed as new. The full 2006 Mason–Shorten paper establishes a common-diagonal-Lyapunov existence criterion for two matrices, not the constrained condition-number budget and optimal logarithmic norm for one four-stage positive cascade. The full 2012 Mason diagonal-Riccati source concerns positive delay systems. A related triangular similarity-norm theorem of Bhatia–Kahan–Li has a substantially different objective; only its public abstract could be inspected, so its body is retained as an explicit residual risk. Searching the exact phase K=2, Jordan chain aliases, matrix measure, metric condition number, and diagonal rate margins located no equivalent or dominating statement. The claim requires the exact all-budget phase law and necessity of the sixth-power threshold, rather than generic diagonal stability or generic numerical-abscissa bounds.
residual_risks: Some older diagonal-stability or matrix-scaling theorem may encode this constrained metric optimization under a different parameterization despite negative exact-form and semantic searches.

value.rationale: Stable positive linear systems always admit some diagonal quadratic Lyapunov function, but an arbitrarily ill-conditioned metric is of limited practical value for controlling observable transients. This theorem solves the first positive chain with three competing link scalings under a natural fixed condition-number budget, shows a nontrivial K=2 optimizer phase transition, and gives the exact sixth-power conditioning price for a nonexpansive semigroup certificate. The profile changes from two constant plateaus to unequal link allocations and is not given by default geometric scaling. The exact rational K=16 obstruction exhibits a meaningful quantitative distinction between Hurwitz stability and a well-conditioned diagonal Lyapunov certificate.
